nodes.title: Provenance staleness: record effective-parent versions per output version, traversing through process nodes
nodes.summary: In a provenance/lineage graph, don't decide staleness per edge (edge.source_version refreshed when the target is saved). When a pipeline has several outputs and only one is regenerated, the refresh of the pipeline's input edges silently marks the siblings fresh. Instead each saved version of a data node records the versions of its effective parents: direct sources plus, through process nodes (pipeline/step/script), the inputs of the process that made it.
nodes.detail: Rules that worked in Sciweave: data node stale if any effective parent's current version != recorded one, or a data parent is itself stale; process nodes are never 'rebuilt', they are flagged 're-run needed' when any of their outputs recorded an older input version; article placements compare placed version vs final/current; informational links (documents/related) never propagate. On new links, setdefault the current versions into the target's latest version (or into all outputs of a process target). A 'cosmetic save' copies the previous version's parents so a font-only re-render stays stale.

nodes.title: Headless Chrome enforces a ~500px minimum window width, so narrow --window-size screenshots show fake overflow
nodes.summary: A --window-size=420,... headless screenshot lays the page out at Chrome's minimum width (~500px) and crops it, so a responsive page looks cut off on the right even when it fits. Verify phone layouts at >=500px or with real device emulation (DevTools / Puppeteer setViewport) before 'fixing' overflow that isn't there.
nodes.trigger: checking a page's mobile/phone layout with headless Chrome or Edge --screenshot at a width under ~500px

nodes.title: Reconstruct a project's analysis history from two independent sources in parallel: files on disk and Claude session transcripts
nodes.summary: To rebuild what was done in a long analysis project, run two read-only agents at once: one mines the folder (README tracker logs, config snapshots, QC reports, file mtimes), the other mines ~/.claude/projects/*.jsonl transcripts (condensed to user+assistant text). They cover different things: the file scan gives the canonical outputs, parameters and article mapping; the transcripts give pre-folder work (e.g. months-earlier legacy runs), dead ends, and dated bug fixes that left no file. Merge them into one tree with a fixed output shape ([id] title (dates) · status / summary / params / paths / feeds / history).
nodes.detail: Ask both agents for the same indented markdown schema so it can be parsed mechanically into an import JSON; refer between entries by stable keys (@key) rather than position numbers, since merging reorders the tree.

nodes.title: Same reference-panel file name across tools does not mean same content: compare bytes before merging
nodes.summary: In the SLE project, FIZI (ssimpsmake/resources/refpanel/g1000_eur.bed, 2.86 GB) and LYNXgwas (refpanels/eur/g1000_eur.bed, 1.25 GB) share file names but are different panels, while LYNXgwas refpanels/{eur,eas,amr} are bit-identical to mrmegask ref_panels/suprefpanels/{eur,eas,amr}. Deduplicating or documenting 'which panel was used' by name would have merged the wrong pair and missed the right one.
nodes.detail: Match by size first (free), then SHA-256 only equal-size files; record one node per identical file set with also_at locations and used_by tools. Implemented as sciweave dedup (scan / check / merge) and enforced in plan check.
nodes.trigger: recording or reusing reference panels / annotation files that appear in several pipelines' folders, or deciding two tools 'used the same panel'

nodes.title: On Windows, atomic save via os.replace fails (WinError 5) while another thread/process has the file open: retry briefly
nodes.summary: A local dashboard server re-reads graph.json constantly; a background job saving it with write-temp + os.replace intermittently failed with PermissionError [WinError 5] Access is denied (about 1 in 4 stress runs). POSIX allows replacing an open file, Windows does not. Wrap the replace, the .bak copy and the read in a short retry loop (e.g. 40 x 50 ms), and give each writer its own temp file name (pid + thread id) so concurrent saves never share one.
nodes.detail: Same session: a job registry dict read by polling requests while worker threads add/update jobs raised 'dictionary changed size during iteration' -- guard adds/updates with a lock and iterate over a snapshot copy.
nodes.domain: python / Windows file I/O / threaded local servers
nodes.trigger: writing a file with temp + os.replace on Windows while a server or another process may be reading it, or iterating a shared dict that background threads modify
